title.narrative: Strengthening Drought Resilience in Zimbabwe: A Collaborative Approach to Anticipatory Actions in Beitbridge, Gwanda, Masvingo, Matobo, and Mwenezi

description.narrative: The projectâ€™s readiness activities are designed to ensure that Mwenezi communities, stakeholders, and systems are prepared to act quickly and effectively when forecasted risks emerge. The main objectives are to strengthen preparedness capacities through training, SOPs, financing mechanisms, and improved coordination; validate and update the Anticipatory Action Plan (AAP) with clear triggers such as rainfall anomalies, river levels, and food price changes; pre-position resources and partnerships with suppliers, communities, and authorities; and enhance community readiness through knowledge, communication tools, and tailored preparedness plans.The project will begin by updating and finalizing the AAP with local stakeholders to ensure its relevance. Activation activities will then address critical needs in water access, livestock health, and agricultural sustainability. At least two high-yield boreholes will be drilled or rehabilitated and fitted with solar technology, supported by water point committees, pump minder training, and conservation awareness. To protect livelihoods, 3,000 beneficiaries (750 households) will receive supplementary feed and veterinary services, alongside training in sustainable livestock management. For food security, the project will support 100 households in poultry and gardens, and provide small grain seed to 250 households, coupled with training in climate-smart agriculture. These actions will diversify incomes, sustain food production, and strengthen resilience.
